design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — delivery_claims task 0 (found parcel kept, behind a late-delivery claim that still owes compensation).

[Step 0 — draw and difficulty pre-check]
draw_counts.py env/env_0031_online_fashion_retailer/tasks/delivery_claims --task 0 -> {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 6]}. --tasks 2 shows task 1 = 2 prerequisite problems, factor counts [4, 5, 6]. Each problem of this tree takes 6 factors.
Base read: products/claims.yaml (6 claim types; events; policies claims_opening, claims_agg_multi_holding, claims_agg_repeat_claims, claims_evt_evidence, claims_evt_carrier_trace, claims_evt_decision, claims_evt_compensation, claims_evt_appeal, claims_evt_recovery, claims_evt_withdrawal), db_schema.json, share_tools.py (find_* per table, verify_customer_identity K=2, transfer_to_human_agent).
Numeric writes the claims tables can carry: claims_opened.claimed_value_usd (a holding that does not yet exist, so it cannot be a computed problem), claims_compensation_issued.amount_usd/quantity, claims_compensation_recovered.amount_usd/quantity, appeal_count. Every problem of every tree must therefore be a compensation or a recovery entry.
BASE CONFLICT NOTED (routed, not edited): every compensation_type of claims_compensation_issued declares a trigger into another category (goodwill_credit -> credit:credit_issued; merchandise_refund/shipping_fee_refund -> orders:orders_payment_refunded; reship -> orders:orders_placed), while the blueprint assigns compensation to this desk's agent. The claims difficulty has no other agent-side numeric write, so the task tools book only the claim-side compensation entry (claim_events) and never write orders or credit rows; the order-level refund and the Goodwill Credit instrument remain the orders/credit desks' writes. No computation of this task reads those triggered rows.
BASE ROUTING NOTED: the blueprint lists the customer's own acts as the non-receipt declaration and withdrawal, neither of which carries a number. The found-parcel charge is a charge to the customer's own card that exists only because the customer chooses to keep the parcel (claims_evt_recovery: "the customer either sends it back ... or is charged for the units kept"), so the customer authorizes it in person (owner=user). The lapsed-window recovery the agent books stays an agent action and is not claimed here.
Space claimed by this task (task 0 is the first; nothing occupied before it): policies claims_ext_late_delivery_refund, claims_ext_late_goodwill, claims_ext_found_parcel_charge; tools book_late_delivery_charge_refund_805d7478, book_late_delivery_goodwill_699f3402, authorize_found_parcel_charge_f3b6f0d4. Left for task 1: the wrong-item keep charge (customer), the delivery-charge refund of a wrong shipment and of an undelivered parcel, i.e. a root plus two prerequisites with their own 4/5/6 factors.

[Design thesis]
Surface goal (customer): keep a parcel refunded as not received that has turned up, and pay for it. Root problem A = claims_ext_found_parcel_charge (customer's own write). Policy prerequisite chain: A is not taken until the compensation owed on the customer's other approved claims has been booked -> the approved Late Delivery Claim on the dress order owes a Goodwill Credit (B = claims_ext_late_goodwill) -> B is fixed only after the delivery-charge refund owed on that claim stands (C = claims_ext_late_delivery_refund). Depth 2 hops; breadth: 18 factors over orders, order lines, payments, loyalty membership and ledger, the Unlimited membership and Goodwill Credits.
Shape: chain C -> B -> A. Edge B<-C value_input (B subtracts the refund C books); edge A<-B state_gate (action form).

[Problem-tree card]
Edge 1: from claims_ext_found_parcel_charge to claims_ext_late_goodwill, kind state_gate, gate claim_events.compensation_type, form action. Prerequisite sentence (rule of A): "A found-parcel charge is not taken until the compensation owed on each of the customer's other approved claims has been booked." Four-point test: negated direction with "not taken until"; XX is a business action (booking owed compensation); no tool/id/code token; scope "each of the customer's other approved claims" = exactly the edge condition. Fallback reason: the compensation owed on another approved claim is booked by different writes depending on its type and delivery charge, so no single record state names one write. Derivation: sentence + records (claim CL approved, no compensation entry) + the Late Delivery rules (refund rule: "An approved Late Delivery Claim on an order whose effective shipping fee was above 0.00 is owed a delivery-charge refund"; goodwill rule: "An approved Late Delivery Claim is owed a Goodwill Credit wherever its make-good amount is not covered by the delivery-charge refund booked on it") -> book both, the Goodwill Credit last. Opening falsity: initial_state.delivery_claims[CL].status = approved, decision_date = 2026-10-08, no claim_events row for that claim. Resolver book_late_delivery_goodwill_699f3402 (agent).
Edge 2: from claims_ext_late_goodwill to claims_ext_late_delivery_refund, kind value_input, gate delivery_refund_booked, form state. Sentence (rule of B): "The Goodwill Credit on a Late Delivery Claim is fixed only after any delivery-charge refund owed on the claim stands on it as a compensation entry." Affirmative direction ("fixed only after"); state = a shipping_fee_refund entry on the claim; only claims_ext_late_delivery_refund writes that entry on a Late Delivery Claim, so the state form resolves to exactly one write. Opening falsity: orders[OL].shipping_fee_usd = 17.00 (> 0, a refund is owed) and no shipping_fee_refund entry on the claim. Resolver book_late_delivery_charge_refund_805d7478 (agent).
Topological order: refund -> goodwill -> found-parcel charge. No parallel edges.
Deletion sensitivity (actual run of _calc): skipping the refund write makes the Goodwill Credit 29.06 instead of 15.48; skipping the goodwill write removes the 15.48 goodwill entry from the terminal DB (the found-parcel charge itself stays 95.56).
user_scenario names neither the late claim's compensation nor any policy id; tools validate nothing (each tool only creates its entry; the claim lookup inside copies customer_id and never refuses).

[Base-invariant card]
claims_compensation_issued is governed by claims_evt_compensation; eligibility approved_only "Compensation is booked only while the claim is in status approved." — satisfied for the late claim by initial_state.delivery_claims[CL].status = approved (system record, pre-action, correlated by claim_id = the call's claim_id). claims_compensation_recovered is governed by claims_evt_recovery; eligibility resolved_only "A recovery is booked only while the claim is in status resolved." — satisfied by initial_state.delivery_claims[CF].status = resolved (resolved 2026-08-13). No time-kind eligibility applies to these subjects. Return window for a found parcel (found_item_return_window_days 14) runs from the turn-up the customer reports (Tuesday 2026-10-06); she keeps it, so the charge path, not the return label, applies.

[Business-object card]
Found-parcel charge: object = Delivered Not Received Claim CF on order OF, line LF (Calloway leather tote, 1 unit). Rows aggregated: claim_events E_FM (merchandise_refund 266.60, qty 1, line LF). Rows excluded: E_FS (shipping_fee_refund 7.53 — delivery refunds are not part of the charge), evidence rows. Late claim object: CL on order OL (Wren silk midi dress, Next Business Day). Delivery-charge refund count reads order_payments: RFS (-7.53, no line, 2026-08-13) counts; RFM (-266.60, line LF) is merchandise and excluded. Goodwill frequency: GC1 (2026-01-29, from claim CP2) counts; GC2 (2025-09-02, from CP3) is 13 months old and excluded.

[Seed rows and why they exist]
customers (identity), loyalty membership (Platinum since 2014-02-10: guarantee refund basis, loyalty courtesy) and 4 ledger earnings (engagement courtesy; 2025-08-18 is the near-miss; balance 1166 = 176+116+496+378), Unlimited Standard Annual (plan supplement; it does not cover Next Business Day, which is why the dress order paid 17.00 = 24.95 - 7.95 Platinum credit), Goodwill Credits GC1/GC2 (frequency multiplier, caps; balances 0.00, no transaction rows), orders OP3/OP2 (older late Expedited 2-Day orders whose claims produced GC2/GC1; their fee was 0.00 because the customer then held Unlimited Express Annual, which covers Expedited 2-Day — shown by the pass ledger: Express Annual fees of 59.00 on 2024-04-14 and 2025-04-14, free-shipping benefit entries on both orders, and the 24.99 Unlimited Standard Annual renewal of 2026-04-14 that applied her downgrade at renewal (pass charter downgrade_effective at_next_renewal); base claims_evt_compensation therefore gave Goodwill Credit, not a fee refund, on those claims), OF (tote, Expedited 2-Day 7.00 fee, tax 19.13 on 255.00), OL (dress, NBD, promised 2026-09-25 Friday, delivered 2026-09-29 Tuesday, tax 15.45 on 206.00), their lines and payments, claims CP3/CP2 (resolved goodwill), CF (resolved DNR: neighbour check, signed declaration, trace no_response, merchandise and delivery refunds on 2026-08-13), CL (approved 2026-10-08, nothing booked). The only unsettled status is CL, which is the object this task's two agent writes handle. Booking compensation does not by itself resolve a claim (stated in both late-claim rules), so no resolution write is owed in this conversation.

[Factor card — claims_ext_late_delivery_refund (gold 13.58, whole baseline 17.00)]
lateness_share (parameter): 2 counted days -> 0.75; baseline 1.0 -> 18.10. delivery_day_count (method): NBD no Saturday delivery -> Monday-to-Friday count 2 (calendar 4); baseline calendar -> 18.10. guarantee_refund_basis (method, multi-source fee record AND loyalty tier, cross-difficulty loyalty): Platinum with fee 17.00 < list 24.95 -> list fee 24.95; baseline fee paid -> 9.25. repeat_refund_share (parameter): 1 parcel-level delivery-claim refund in 12 months -> 0.75; baseline -> 18.10 (near-miss: the line-level 266.60 refund). reporting_share (parameter): 8 days -> 0.90; baseline -> 15.09. refunded_delivery_tax (method): OH delivery-taxing -> tax at 15.45/206.00; baseline none -> 12.63.
[Factor card — claims_ext_late_goodwill (gold 15.48, whole baseline 0)]
lateness_amount (method): 4 calendar days -> per-day accrual 16.00; baseline 10.00 -> 9.86. unlimited_plan_supplement: Standard Annual -> 5.00; baseline 0 -> 10.79. order_value_supplement: 189.00 -> 5.00; baseline -> 10.79. service_supplement: NBD -> 5.00; baseline -> 10.79. shopping_relationship (multi-source XSUM spend AND XCOUNT orders): 495.00 on 3 orders -> 1.25; baseline -> 9.67 (near-miss: the August 2025 order). goodwill_frequency (cross-difficulty credit): 1 credit -> 0.75; baseline -> 25.17 (near-miss GC2).
[Factor card — claims_ext_found_parcel_charge (gold 95.56, whole baseline 266.60)]
seasonal_charge_base (method): regular line, 72 days -> 248.00 x 0.70 untaxed; baseline compensation 266.60 -> 149.96. loyalty_courtesy (multi-source tier AND membership months, cross-difficulty loyalty): 0.15; baseline -> 115.09. engagement_courtesy (cross-difficulty loyalty ledger): 3 earnings -> 0.02; baseline -> 98.16 (near-miss 2025-08-18). service_courtesy: Expedited 2-Day -> 0.05; baseline -> 102.07. recovery_share: 56 days -> 0.75; baseline -> 129.41. label_saving: accessories 6.00; baseline -> 101.56.
Overwrites declared: claims_evt_compensation (refund sentence; goodwill "instead" clause) and claims_evt_recovery (found-parcel sentence). Base params stay in force (late_delivery_goodwill_usd is the make-good default; credit caps are read from the credit charter).

[Persona design]
Rosalind Wexley, chatty, honest librarian; volunteers only the turned-up tote and the wish to keep and pay ("I'd like to keep it and pay for it rather than send it back"); gives email, then mobile when asked; never states amounts; agrees passively if told something must be settled first; answers about the late dress only if asked; runs the hand-over once with the given values; closes after the charge is confirmed. No ask beyond the root request.

[Standard solution]
Locate by email, verify (email + mobile), read claims, claim events, orders, lines, payments, loyalty membership and ledger, Unlimited membership, credit instruments. Discover that the found-parcel charge waits on the approved late claim's compensation; book the delivery-charge refund 13.58 on CL, then the Goodwill Credit 15.48 on CL, then unlock and hand over the found-parcel charge 95.56 on CF line LF, 1 unit, which the customer authorizes.

[Verification]
Commands: python3 _gen0.py; python3 _task0.py; .venv/bin/python _calc.py tasks/0.json (temporary authoring scripts, removed after closing). Output: claims_ext_late_delivery_refund expected 13.58 baseline 17.0; claims_ext_late_goodwill expected 15.48 baseline 0; claims_ext_found_parcel_charge expected 95.56 baseline 266.6; skip refund -> goodwill 29.06. Per-task gates: see the final gate run of the difficulty.
Draft recomputation from the visible context (rules as published, tool schemas, finder returns, persona lines) reaches the same three writes, objects and amounts; the only judgement left to the reader is which other claims count as approved with compensation owed, and the records show exactly one (CL).


[Rework round 2 — audit audits/policy_task/delivery_claims (0.md, _difficulty.md)]
F-1 symptom: delivery_day_count's Monday-to-Saturday tier could never be taken by an approved Late Delivery Claim (the only Saturday non-courier service, Economy Ground, is not guaranteed). Root cause: ladder drawn over service attributes rather than over the guaranteed services. Change: tiers are now (a) Expedited 2-Day order shipped to Alaska or Hawaii -> Monday-to-Friday days less the one-day island transit allowance (Expedited 2-Day is the only guaranteed service available there), (b) any other order on a service without Saturday delivery -> Monday-to-Friday days, (c) otherwise (Same-Day Courier) -> calendar days; all three are reachable. This world sits on (b) as before; recomputed values unchanged.
F-2 symptom: the basis tier said "because a free-shipping credit was taken off" while compute tested only fee < list fee. Change: rule and compute now both require the fee paid to equal the list fee less the service's free_shipping_credit_usd (ABS(...) < 0.005); a Same-Day fee cut by a plan discount now falls through, as the rule says. Values unchanged here.
F-3 symptom: taxable-share states without gift-card lines fell to "no tax". Change: tier (b) now covers every order to a taxable-share state, scaled by the share of taxable (non-gift-card) merchandise; only orders to states that do not tax delivery get no tax. OH remains tier (a); values unchanged.
F-4 symptom: the two older Expedited orders carried a 0.00 fee that the seeded Standard Annual plan could not produce. Change: pass_ledger rows added (Express Annual charges 2024/2025, both free-shipping benefits, the 2026 Standard Annual renewal) and a find_pass_ledger read (step 10); the rationale sentence above now states the plan history the seed shows. Write steps renumbered to 13/15/17; values unchanged.
O-1: late refund owed when fee and surcharge together exceed 0.00; none when both are 0.00. O-4: the found-parcel rule restates "A found-parcel charge is booked only while the claim is in status resolved."; the undelivered refund is owed on merchandise-refund claims only. O-5: rules now say "units compensated on that line, all of which the customer keeps" and "returns in status settled whose settled date falls in the trailing 12 calendar months". O-6: tool docstrings say "to the nearest cent" (no half-up claim); no scored value sits on a half cent. O-9: the repeat and history counts read refunds "as they stand on the orders' payment records". O-2/O-3/O-8: no change needed (base orders ground no edge; field gates are stated by the rule sentence; baseline-in-rule structure). O-7: kept — the list-fee basis is the stated delivery-promise refund for members whose fee was reduced by their own free-shipping credit, and the service courtesy reflects the premium the customer paid for speed.
Re-run after the changes: see the gate block of the round-2 closure.
user_scenario: You are Rosalind Wexley, 44, a school librarian in Upper Arlington, Ohio, calling Marlowe & Finch customer care by phone on a Thursday afternoon. You are friendly, a little sheepish and very honest, and you speak in full, chatty sentences. Back in August you ordered a cognac leather tote — the Calloway tote — and the tracking said it was delivered, but it never reached you. You reported it, signed the declaration they asked for, and Marlowe & Finch refunded you for it in the middle of August. This Tuesday your neighbour two houses down, who had been travelling for weeks, knocked on your door with the parcel: it had been left on her porch all along. You open the call by explaining exactly that and saying: "The tote I was refunded for has turned up, and honestly I love it — I'd like to keep it and pay for it rather than send it back." That is the only thing you are calling about. When the representative asks who you are, you give your email, rosalind.wexley@gmail.com, and, if a second detail is asked for, your mobile number, 6145550193. You do not know any order, claim or line reference by heart and say so if asked; you are happy for them to look it up. You have no idea what keeping the tote will cost and you never suggest a figure; if the representative asks what you expect to pay, you say you'll leave that to them. If the representative asks whether you would rather send the tote back with a prepaid label, you say no, you would really like to keep it. If the representative tells you that something else on your account has to be settled or booked first before they can take a charge, you simply say that is fine and they should go ahead; you do not ask what it is or why, and you do not bring up any other order yourself. If they ask about another delivery of yours, you answer only what you remember: the emerald silk dress you ordered with next-day delivery at the end of September came several days late, and you already reported that. When the representative tells you the amount and hands you the step to authorize the charge to your card yourself, you run it exactly once with exactly the claim number, line reference, number of items and amount they give you, without changing anything. If the amount sounds lower than the price you paid, you say that is very kind and do not argue; you never try to correct their arithmetic. Once the charge has gone through and the representative confirms it, you thank them warmly and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_id: Value f36b9b33-01e3-45ab-906f-6823be66436b. Basis: find_delivery_claims returns this Late Delivery Claim with status approved, decision_date 2026-10-08 and no compensation entry in find_claim_events; the policy rule says 'An approved Late Delivery Claim on an order whose effective shipping fee was above 0.00 is owed a delivery-charge refund, booked as one shipping fee refund entry on the claim for the whole parcel.' Uniqueness: the customer's other claims are resolved (the tote claim and two older Late Delivery Claims), so this is the only approved claim; its order 0f630098-2732-4dd1-afa6-bf28c0972270 carries a fee of 17.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: Value 13.58. Guarantee refund basis: fee 17.00 is above 0.00 and equals the Next Business Day list fee 24.95 less its 7.95 free-shipping credit (nothing else was taken off), active tier Marlowe Rewards Platinum -> list fee 24.95 + surcharge 0.00 (the computation document alone gives 17.00). edges.condition: Every other claim of the customer in status approved carries every compensation entry this charter owes on it; for an approved Late Delivery Claim that is its delivery-charge refund entry and its Goodwill Credit entry where one is owed.
edges.policy_source: A found-parcel charge is not taken until the compensation owed on each of the customer's other approved claims has been booked.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The Late Delivery Claim on the dress order is approved (decided 2026-10-08) and carries no compensation entry at all, although its delivery-charge refund and Goodwill Credit are owed.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: After step 13 books the delivery-charge refund (13.58) and step 15 books the Goodwill Credit (15.48) on that claim, every approved claim other than the tote claim carries its owed compensation.

edges.condition: The Late Delivery Claim carries a claims_compensation_issued entry of type shipping_fee_refund for the delivery-charge refund its order's fee owes, or the order's fee and surcharge were 0.00 so that none is owed.
edges.policy_source: The Goodwill Credit on a Late Delivery Claim is fixed only after any delivery-charge refund owed on the claim stands on it as a compensation entry.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The order's effective fee is 17.00, so a delivery-charge refund is owed, but the claim carries no shipping_fee_refund entry.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 13 creates the shipping_fee_refund entry of 13.58 on the claim; delivery_refund_booked rises from 0.00 to 13.58.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (found-parcel charge <- Goodwill Credit <- delivery-charge refund); every pair is ordered by a prerequisite sentence, so there is no free reordering: the Goodwill Credit is fixed only after the delivery-charge refund stands (it subtracts that refund), and the found-parcel charge is not taken until the late claim's owed compensation is booked.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the Goodwill Credit write leaves the terminal DB without the goodwill_credit entry of 15.48 on the Late Delivery Claim, so the terminal hash differs; the found-parcel charge itself reads only the tote claim and stays 95.56.

Skipping the delivery-charge refund write leaves delivery_refund_booked at 0.00, so the Goodwill Credit recomputes to 29.06 instead of 15.48, and the shipping_fee_refund entry of 13.58 is missing from the terminal DB.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only keeping the turned-up tote and paying for it. It never names the Late Delivery Claim's compensation, a delivery-charge refund or a Goodwill Credit, and contains none of the policy ids claims_ext_late_goodwill or claims_ext_late_delivery_refund. The dress order is mentioned only as a passive answer if the agent asks about another delivery, and the customer agrees to 'something else being settled first' only after the agent says so, without asking what it is.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: authorize_found_parcel_charge_f3b6f0d4 creates the recovery entry with ctx.create and returns its receipt without reading the status of any other claim; book_late_delivery_goodwill_699f3402 creates the goodwill entry without reading whether a delivery-charge refund exists; book_late_delivery_charge_refund_805d7478 creates the refund entry unconditionally. The only read in any of them is a lookup of the claim row that copies the claim's customer_id onto the new entry and never refuses.
